title: LibreChat-AI/LibreChat — Enhanced ChatGPT Clone: Features Agents, MCP, Skills, DeepSeek, Anthropic, AWS, OpenAI, Responses API, Azure, Groq, o1, GPT-5, Mistral, OpenRouter, Vertex AI, Gemini, Artifacts, AI model switching, message search, Code Interpreter, langchain, DALL-E-3, OpenAPI Actions, Functions, Secure Multi-User Auth, Presets, open-source for self-hosting. Active
content:
English · 中文
- Agent Management API (beta): Create, discover, update, and delete Agents; manage Agent files and Skills; and authenticate machine clients through deployment-bound OIDC identities while preserving existing role and Agent access controls. Public OpenAPI and Swagger UI cover inference, events, Agent management, and Skill management.
- Attached workspaces (highly experimental): Select or save a per-Agent default workspace for each managed or personal code worker, then let Agents inspect trees, read and search files, author changes, and run Bash with bounded timeouts. Personal workers support bounded self-service enrollment, readiness status, and per-Agent Git identity.
- Background tool controls: Optionally cancel ordinary background tools, including attached Bash, while keeping detached Subagent execution independent.
- Code approval controls: Choose Ask, Allow, or Deny for file writes and command execution where administrators permit it, including a Full access mode for trusted attached environments. File Search and Run Code also honor role grants.
- Manual context compaction: Start a summarize-only turn before the context window fills while preserving recent conversation content according to the deployment's summarization policy.
- Context Usage: Inspect dialogue, retained tool traffic, Agent instructions, cache, cost, and runway pressure without double-counting category subsets.
- Unified attachments: Upload once and let LibreChat route content to the model or extracted text, then provision File Search and Code tools only when needed.
- Models: Added GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, with Responses API routing and tool-call support.
- Agent and chat UI: Unified tool activity, reasoning, search, and Agent workflows; added one draggable Pinned section for chats and favorites, morphing state icons, high-contrast themes, rich-text message copying, clearer sidebar titles, and refined live phase layouts.
- Observability: Inspect ordered model conversations, tool rounds, and costs in the Trace Viewer; export correlated application logs through OpenTelemetry, configure allowlisted Langfuse trace identity and metadata, tag browser diagnostics with client build IDs, and scope Insights to authorized Agents.
- Reliability and security: Strengthened Agent continuation and checkpoint recovery, Redis liveness detection, DocumentDB coordination, OpenID and MCP OAuth sessions, shared-link throttling, tenant isolation, attachment bounds, and upload error handling.
Read the full v0.8.8 changelog.
- 🖥️ UI & Experience inspired by ChatGPT with enhanced design and features

  - Seamless File Handling: Upload, process, and download files directly
  - No Privacy Concerns: Fully isolated and secure execution
  - Open-Source & Self-Hostable: powered by ClickHouse/code-interpreter
- 🔦 Agents & Tools Integration: 
  - LibreChat Agents:
    - No-Code Custom Assistants: Build specialized, AI-driven helpers
    - Agent Marketplace: Discover and deploy community-built agents
    - Collaborative Sharing: Share agents with specific users and groups
    - Flexible & Extensible: Use MCP Servers, tools, file search, code execution, and more
    - Skills: Create reusable SKILL.md instruction bundles for manual, automatic, or always-on agent workflows
    - Agent Plugins: Experimentally bundle deployment Skills and MCP servers into startup-loaded packages
    - Subagents: Delegate focused work to isolated child agent runs with their own context windows
    - Agent Management API: Automate Agent, file, and Skill management with deployment-bound OIDC clients
    - Attached Code Workspaces: Let Agents inspect, search, edit, and run commands in managed or personal workspaces (highly experimental)
    - Compatible with Custom Endpoints, OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google, Vertex AI, Responses API, and more
    - Model Context Protocol (MCP) Support for Tools
- 🔍 Web Search: 
  - Search the internet and retrieve relevant information to enhance your AI context
  - Combines search providers, content scrapers, and result rerankers for optimal results
  - Customizable Jina Reranking: Configure custom Jina API URLs for reranking services
  - Learn More →
- 🪄 Generative UI with Code Artifacts: 
  - Code Artifacts create React, HTML, and Mermaid content directly in chat
  - Open previews fullscreen and export Mermaid diagrams as SVG or PNG
- 🎨 Image Generation & Editing 
  - Text-to-image and image-to-image with GPT-Image-1

report.summary: LibreChat v0.8.8 turns the open-source ChatGPT clone into a full agent platform, adding an Agent Management API, attached code workspaces, MCP tools, Skills and enterprise observability.
report.background: LibreChat began as a self-hosted, multi-provider alternative to ChatGPT's interface, letting teams point one familiar UI at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, Azure or local models like Ollama. Over the past two years the chat-front-end category has shifted from simple model switching toward agentic workflows: tool calling, code execution, retrieval and long-running tasks. Two standards accelerated this — Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool interoperability, and the OpenAI Responses API for stateful tool-call routing. Meanwhile enterprises want these capabilities without sending data to a vendor-controlled SaaS, and with SSO, RBAC, audit logs and cost tracking. LibreChat's v0.8.8 release answers that demand by layering a machine-facing management API, sandboxed workspaces, reusable instruction bundles and production observability onto a codebase that is already Docker-deployable and multi-user. The result is less a ChatGPT clone and more an open agent runtime with a chat UI attached.
key_points: Agent Management API (beta): teams can now create, discover, update and delete Agents programmatically, manage their files and Skills, and authenticate machine clients through deployment-bound OIDC identities — all while inheriting existing role and Agent access controls. A public OpenAPI spec and Swagger UI cover inference, events, Agent and Skill management, making LibreChat scriptable in CI/CD pipelines.

Attached code workspaces (highly experimental) let an Agent pick a default workspace, inspect file trees, read and search files, author edits and run Bash with bounded timeouts. Administrators get Ask/Allow/Deny approval controls for writes and command execution, including a Full-access mode for trusted environments, plus the ability to cancel background tools without killing detached Subagents.

Skills and Agent Plugins introduce reusable SKILL.md instruction bundles that run manually, automatically or always-on, and can be packaged with MCP servers into startup-loaded plugins. Combined with the Agent Marketplace, collaborative sharing, MCP tool support and Subagents with isolated context windows, this is a no-code path to specialized assistants.

Context and model handling got serious upgrades: unified attachments route uploads to the model or to extracted text and only provision File Search/Code tools when needed; manual context compaction summarizes before the window fills; and the new Context Usage panel itemizes dialogue, retained tool traffic, instructions, cache, cost and runway without double counting.

Observability and reliability: a Trace Viewer shows ordered model conversations, tool rounds and costs; logs export via OpenTelemetry with allowlisted Langfuse trace identity; and hardening covers Agent checkpoint recovery, Redis liveness detection, OpenID/MCP OAuth sessions, tenant isolation, shared-link throttling and upload bounds.
report.impact: For the AI industry, LibreChat is converging on the same architecture as commercial agent platforms — managed agents, MCP tooling, sandboxed execution, OAuth-bound machine identity — but as open source. That pressures closed vendors on price and lock-in, and gives enterprises a compliance-friendly option when regulated data cannot leave their infrastructure. For developers, the biggest shift is the Agent Management API plus MCP and Skills: agents become versioned, deployable artifacts instead of hand-configured chats, and Bash/code workspaces make LibreChat a runtime for real tasks, not just conversation. The approval controls and trace viewer are the guardrails that make that acceptable to security teams. For regular users, the payoff is a single interface across GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and local models, with artifacts, image generation, file chat, speech and resumable streams — self-hosted and free, though workspace features remain experimental and should be piloted carefully.
report.tools: Start with LibreChat itself (Docker Compose for one-command setup, or the bundled admin panel for user/role management). Follow the Model Context Protocol spec and reference MCP servers to add tools. ClickHouse/code-interpreter powers sandboxed multi-language execution. Pair with Ollama or LM Studio for local models, Langfuse and OpenTelemetry for tracing, and Jina for reranking. LibreChat's own OpenAPI/Swagger endpoint is the entry point for automating agents.
